AC Repair in Fulshear, TX, When the House and the System Are Both New

In Fulshear the air conditioner is often only a few years old, and the paperwork that came with the house can matter as much as the repair. Call the free line any hour to reach a locally owned heating and cooling contractor that takes Fulshear jobs.

Searching for AC repair in Fulshear, TX, usually means something has gone wrong with a fairly young system in a fairly young house. That changes the order of the steps: on a new home, the right first call may be to your builder, not to a repair company. This page walks through that order, and through how the free line can connect you with a local contractor when you do need one.

Houston Air & Heating is a call line. It owns no tools and sends no crews. Fulshear: a small Fort Bend town surrounded by new neighborhoods

Fulshear sits in western Fort Bend County, on the far west side of the Houston area. The 2020 Census counted 16,856 residents, up from 1,134 in 2010, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 64,630. Between 2024 and 2025 it ranked second among the fastest growing U.S. cities of 20,000 people or more. Large master planned communities have grown up around the old town center, and a big share of the homes here were built recently. For heating and cooling, that has a practical upshot: many systems are still inside their warranty periods, many have never had a full season of maintenance, and many owners have never needed a repair before.

New does not mean trouble free. A system installed during construction was set up in a house with no furniture, no family and often no summer yet. The first real August is when hidden installation problems tend to show up.

From plantation stop to boomtown

The town's name comes from Churchill Fulshear, one of Stephen F. Austin's Old Three Hundred colonists, who settled on land granted by Mexico in 1824. His son gave a railroad a right of way through the family land in 1888, and the town site was laid out in 1890. For most of the twentieth century Fulshear stayed a small farm town of a few hundred people or fewer, until Houston's growth reached it beginning in the 1970s. The city incorporated in 1977 and is now a home rule city.

That history explains the housing mix. A handful of older homes sit near the original town center, but with the population growing from about a thousand people in 2010 to tens of thousands today, most Fulshear houses are recent builds on former ranch and farm land. If your home is one of them, its heating and cooling system is probably the first one the house has ever had.

Who supplies what in Fulshear

  • Electric wiresCenterPoint Energy delivers electricity in Fulshear and handles outages. You pick your own retail electric provider, and the city points residents to Power to Choose to compare plans. The city does not sell power.
  • Natural gasThe city lists two gas companies: CenterPoint Energy and Si Energy. Which one serves you depends on your neighborhood, so check the name on your gas bill before you need it in an emergency.
  • City utilitiesThe City of Fulshear bills water, sewer and trash.
  • PermitsThe city requires a permit to replace a mechanical system, both inside city limits and in its extraterritorial jurisdiction, and takes applications through an online portal.

Three warranties to check before you pay for a repair

The exact terms are in your closing papers and equipment booklets. These are the questions to answer first.

The builder warranty

Covers workmanship for a set time after closing. A duct that came loose, a drain line with no slope or a refrigerant joint that leaks from day one may fall here. Report it the way the warranty asks, usually in writing.

The equipment warranty

Covers parts from the manufacturer. Some makers offer a longer term only if the unit was registered online within a short window after installation. Find the model and serial numbers and check the maker's website.

The labor coverage

A parts warranty rarely pays for the hours to install the part. Find out whether the original installer covers labor, and for how long, before you agree to a bill.

Problems that show up in a new home's first summers

  • A drain line that backs up. If the condensate line was not sloped or trapped well, water collects and a safety float switch shuts the system off. Look for water in the pan under the indoor unit.
  • A warm upstairs. Dampers that were never adjusted after move-in, or ducts that were pinched during construction, can starve upstairs rooms of air.
  • A filter clogged fast. Fine construction dust keeps settling for months. Check the filter monthly the first year and change it when it looks gray.
  • A system that never shuts off. On the hottest afternoons long run times can be normal. A change from last summer, or rooms that will not get below the high 70s, is worth a service call.
  • A room that has never cooled. If it has been warm since the day you moved in, it is likely a design or installation issue, which points back to the builder warranty.

Safe checks before you call

Set the thermostat to Cool and a few degrees below the room temperature, and replace its batteries if the screen is blank. Pull the filter and swap it if it is dirty. If the outdoor unit is silent, check for a tripped breaker and reset it a single time; if it trips again, leave it alone. Clear away grass clippings, toys or bags that have blown against the outdoor unit. Anything involving refrigerant, wiring or the gas furnace is for a technician.

A gas odor indoors means everyone walks out first; phone 911 and the gas utility only once you are clear of the house. CenterPoint Energy lists 888-876-5786 for reporting a gas leak in the Houston area; if Si Energy serves your street, use the emergency number on its bill. The same goes for a sounding carbon monoxide detector: out of the house, then 911.

Permits when a system is replaced

The City of Fulshear's rule is broad: anyone who plans to replace an electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system within the city limits or the ETJ must apply to the Building Official and get a permit first. The exemptions are narrow, such as portable heaters, portable cooling units and a minor part that does not change how the equipment was approved. A full change out of an air conditioner or furnace is not on that list. The city takes trade permit applications, including HVAC, through its online portal, and its inspectors work weekdays. Before you sign, find out which side applies for the permit and whether the final inspection is included in the price.

Planning ahead for the first replacement

Builders usually choose equipment that meets the code minimum for efficiency. That is perfectly workable. When the first replacement comes due years from now, it is a chance to ask about two stage or variable speed equipment, which can run longer at low speed and pull more moisture out of the air in Fort Bend's sticky summers. Keep a folder with the model numbers, install date and every service invoice, because the next contractor will ask.

Common questions

My Fulshear house is two years old and the AC stopped cooling. Who do I call first?

Look at your builder warranty before anything else. Problems in the first years of a new home, such as a loose duct or a badly sloped drain line, may be the builder's responsibility, and many warranties ask you to report them in writing. If the warranty does not cover it, or you need help right away, call the line to reach a local contractor.

Will a repair by another company void my new AC's warranty?

Read the warranty booklet and ask the builder or equipment maker before work starts. Terms differ, and some require repairs to be done a certain way or by a certain contractor. Keep every invoice and write down the model and serial numbers from the outdoor and indoor units.

Why is the upstairs of my new Fulshear home so much warmer than downstairs?

Heat rises, and upstairs rooms sit right under a hot attic. In a new house the cause is often airflow that was never balanced after move-in, closed or misset dampers, or a system sized without a room by room load calculation. A technician can measure airflow at each vent before anyone suggests new equipment.

Does Fulshear require a permit for a new AC system?

Yes, in most cases. The City of Fulshear says anyone replacing a mechanical system inside the city limits or in its extraterritorial jurisdiction, the ETJ, must first get a permit from the city's Building Official. Only small jobs, such as swapping a minor part, are exempt. Ask the contractor to apply through the city's online portal and to list the permit on the quote.

Can I get AC repair in Fulshear on a weekend?

The line answers every day and night. It takes your details and connects you with a local, independently owned contractor that works in Fulshear. Ask that contractor about its weekend availability and any after-hours charge before it comes out.
